title: Pin Vercel function region to Turso's region
description:
MEASURED IN PRODUCTION: https://www.remfo.app returns Server-Timing 'auth;desc="session db";dur=256.0' on every request. That is ONE Turso round trip measured from the edge. Locally a bare 'SELECT 1' against Turso is 296ms while the /record list query is 297ms, so the database work is ~1ms and essentially all of it is network.

Protected pages pay this round trip TWICE, serially: hooks.server.ts validates the session (256ms), and only then does load run its query (another 256ms). Streaming does not remove either trip, it just delivers the second one later over JS.

CAUSE: svelte.config.js uses adapter({ runtime: 'edge' }) with no regions. Edge functions run near the VIEWER, which for a single-region database maximises distance on the hot path, twice per request.

FIX: pin regions to the Turso database's region. Verify adapter-vercel's regions option applies to the edge runtime before relying on it. Needs the production DB region, which is not readable from this machine (the turso CLI is not installed and .env.local points at dev-remfo-xerosanyam, a dev database).

WHY P1: this is roughly half a second off every protected page, and it dissolves the /record stream-vs-await decision in remfo-11v.4 rather than forcing a permanent tradeoff to work around a config line.

ALSO FOUND: the module-level session cache in hooks.server.ts never hits in production. Every request reported desc='session db', never 'session cache'. On edge the instances are too short-lived for it to pay off.
acceptance_criteria: Production Server-Timing 'auth' duration drops substantially from 256ms, measured on www.remfo.app. /record then re-measured both ways with the new numbers.
notes:
RESOLVED, and the region pin was not the fix, though it is now correct and worth keeping.

ROOT CAUSE: TURSO_CONNECTION_URL pointed at the LEGACY hostname libsql://remfo-xerosanyam.turso.io, which Turso still serves from its old Fly infrastructure and which proxies through San Jose. The database itself was in aws-ap-south-1 (Mumbai) the whole time. Every query flew Mumbai -> California -> Mumbai.

That legacy hop is what produced 'fly-request-id: ...-sjc' on every probe, which I twice misread as the database's own location. The user correctly pushed back both times.

EVIDENCE the switch was data-safe, checked before recommending it: both hostnames returned identical counts (cards 1929, users 452, activity 6985, newest 1788294341). Same database, two routes.

FIX: production TURSO_CONNECTION_URL changed to libsql://remfo-xerosanyam.aws-ap-south-1.turso.io.

MEASURED AFTER DEPLOY, 6 samples from a function confirmed running in bom1:
  db;desc="SELECT 1";dur=1.0 to 4.0ms  (was 260ms)
  shell;dur=2.0 to 5.0ms                (was 261ms)
About 130x on the round trip. Protected pages pay it twice serially, so roughly half a second per authenticated page load.

NOTE: do NOT mirror this in .env.local. The dev machine is in California where the legacy route is genuinely faster (297ms vs 915ms measured). Local and production want opposite hostnames.
close_reason: Root cause was a legacy Turso hostname proxying via San Jose, not the region. Fixed by switching the production connection string; SELECT 1 from bom1 went 260ms -> 2ms. Region pin retained and now correct.

title: Reduce revise DOM and aggregate measure activity
description: Implement measured low-hanging performance improvements: bound the /revise review batch instead of rendering all due cards, and aggregate /measure activity by date/action in SQL instead of sending every activity row to the browser.
acceptance_criteria: Revise renders a bounded batch while retaining meaningful progress; measure uses aggregated daily data without breaking streak/heatmaps; focused tests, full tests, build, and affected Lighthouse audits pass or show measured improvement.
notes: Implemented and measured. /revise now fetches at most 50 due cards, mounts only the current card, advances locally, and invalidates after a completed batch. Versus 2026-08-31 22:35 mobile baseline: performance 76.3->90.7, load 1193->678ms, FCP 2186->1314ms, LCP 4426->3299ms, TBT 213->24ms, bytes 192->121KB, DOM 22275->89. /measure now performs one SQL group-by action/day query and sends daily counts rather than every activity event; totals remain exact and streak accepts the daily dates. Mobile performance 77.3->80.7, FCP 2774->2052ms, LCP 4451->3889ms, bytes 240->223KB; desktop performance 99->100 and load 728->423ms. Mobile load comparison had a cold-session outlier, so not treated as regression evidence. 46 tests, production build, formatting, and diff checks pass. Existing MSW test warnings and PWA glob warning remain unrelated.
close_reason: Reduced revise DOM/query payload and aggregated measure activity, with tests/build and Lighthouse evidence.

title: Validate and minimize record optimizations
description: Benchmark the record index and LIMIT+1 pagination against the original exact-count behavior. Preserve exact card totals unless removing them has a meaningful measured performance benefit. Revert any optimization not justified by evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Directly compare query plans/timings; retain only justified changes; restore exact count if LIMIT+1 benefit is marginal; tests and build pass.
notes: Direct read-only Turso A/B, 10 alternating samples: exact cards+COUNT in parallel avg 325ms (298-411); LIMIT+1 avg 326ms (296-410). No benefit, so restored exact total and original UI. Index A/B, 10 alternating samples: indexed avg 340ms (299-484); forced scan avg 346ms (300-443), only 6ms difference and below network variance. Removed schema/migration and dropped the development DB index. Verified retained optimizations: 50-card bounded query, parallel exact count, streamed promise, previous-list display during reload, and all-page isolated perf runner. 46 tests and production build pass; diff check clean.
close_reason: Benchmarked both changes and fully reverted them as unjustified; retained only previously proven pagination, streaming, and perf-runner improvements.

title: Audit record performance and test all pages by default
description: Audit /record for actionable performance optimizations. Update the perf harness to discover every SvelteKit page route by default, safely skip logout/endpoints/dynamic routes, handle public and authenticated pages correctly, and isolate every Lighthouse sample from cache/service-worker state.
acceptance_criteria: Default perf discovers all concrete +page routes and runs mobile+desktop; public pages remain logged out and protected pages authenticated; each sample uses isolated browser state; /record audit findings are documented with evidence and follow-up tracking.
notes: Completed audit and runner expansion. Default route discovery now covers every concrete +page route: /, /compare/anki, /learn, /measure, /pricing, /record, /revise; route groups are stripped, dynamic directories and /logout are skipped. Each Lighthouse sample uses an isolated browser context; auth cookie is set only for protected routes, preventing service-worker/cache/session contamination. Smoke validation: public / mobile isolated load=91ms, /record mobile isolated load=1166ms with getCards/getTotalCards about 309ms; all Lighthouse categories were 100, but /record correctly failed the 100ms observed-load budget. Record findings: remote Turso/auth work dominates; cards query filters user_id+deleted and sorts created_at without a matching composite index; exact count adds a second DB query; 50-card result yields about 1212 DOM nodes/134KB but TBT is negligible, so DB/index/query work is the priority. Validation: node --check, prettier check, git diff --check, and 46 Vitest tests pass. Pre-existing MSW warnings remain.
close_reason: Implemented all-page default audits with isolated page samples and completed evidence-backed /record audit.

title: Add average page-load budgets and clear perf verdicts
description: Make perf output concise, average all runs instead of using medians, record observed navigation load time, enforce a 100ms average load budget per requested page/device, and summarize whether the current label is GOOD, BAD, MIXED, or unchanged versus the previous label.
acceptance_criteria: Three-run reports use arithmetic averages; output includes page load duration, PASS/FAIL against 100ms, and an overall comparison verdict; any budget failure makes a live run exit nonzero after all requested audits; auto-build suppresses non-actionable Vite warnings.
notes: Fresh three-run validation: average observed load 686ms from 1256/398/404ms, correctly failed the 100ms budget and exited 1. Internal Vite build output is quiet. Comparison verdict is forced BAD on any budget failure. Threshold applies independently to every path supplied via --pages.
close_reason: Added arithmetic averages, observed page-load timing, 100ms per-page/device budget gate, nonzero failure exit, concise builds, and explicit verdicts.

title: Deploy the /revise fixes: ContentRenderer probe and contrast are fixed locally but not shipped
description: /revise is the worst page in the app at mobile performance 77 and best-practices 77, and both causes are already fixed in the working tree but uncommitted. The ContentRenderer network probe (see closed remfo-os3) is responsible for the best-practices 77 on both form factors and contributes to 740ms mobile TBT. The 882 colour-contrast failures are fixed in Card.svelte, CardGroup.svelte and ReviewProgress.svelte. Uncommitted files: src/lib/components/ContentRenderer.svelte, src/lib/components/ContentRenderer.test.ts, src/lib/components/Cards/Card.svelte, src/lib/components/Cards/CardGroup.svelte, src/lib/components/Cards/ReviewProgress.svelte.
acceptance_criteria: After deploy, /revise mobile: best-practices 100, third-party-cookies and inspector-issues pass, colour-contrast passes, TBT materially below 740ms.

title: Security: patch sveltekit-superforms prototype pollution and adapter-vercel cache poisoning
description: Found by bun audit. (1) sveltekit-superforms <=2.27.3 has high-severity prototype pollution in parseFormData (GHSA-hwmc-4c8j-xxj7). Repo is on 2.16.1 and every superValidate(event, ...) call in src/lib/actions/card.action.ts, learn/, record/ and revise/+page.server.ts feeds attacker-controlled form data through it. (2) @sveltejs/adapter-vercel <6.3.2 has moderate cache poisoning (GHSA-9pq4-5hcf-288c); repo is on 5.4.1 and deploys to Vercel. Remaining audit hits are transitive dev tooling only (qs via cypress, brace-expansion via eslint/tailwind/svelte-check, valibot via the superforms adapter this app does not use).
design: sveltekit-superforms 2.16.1 -> 2.30.2, zod 3.23.8 -> 3.25.76, @sveltejs/adapter-vercel 5.4.1 -> 6.3.4. No Zod 4 migration needed: patched superforms peers zod '^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0', so staying on the zod 3 line keeps the existing zod() adapter import unchanged. adapter-vercel 6 peers @sveltejs/kit ^2.4.0 and the repo is on 2.5.18, so no kit bump. Three version strings, no code changes expected.
acceptance_criteria: bun audit reports no advisories against direct dependencies. bun run test and bun run build pass. Add, review and delete a card in the deployed app to confirm superValidate still works.

title: No CI: tests have never run on a push or PR
description: No .github/ directory exists, despite a pull_request_template.md. bun run test, check, and lint have only ever run locally.
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs bun install, bun run test, bun run check, bun run lint on push and PR, and is green.

title: bun run lint is dead: eslint 9 with an eslintrc config
description: eslint 9.7.0 is installed but config is .eslintrc.cjs. npx eslint . exits with 'ESLint couldn't find an eslint.config.(js|mjs|cjs) file'. The lint half of the script has never run since the v9 bump. Prettier half still works.
design: Migrate to eslint.config.js flat config, or pin eslint to ^8. Flat config preferred, eslint-plugin-svelte 2.43 supports it.
acceptance_criteria: npx eslint . runs and reports real results (exit 0 or genuine lint errors).
notes: Migrated legacy .eslintrc.cjs/.eslintignore to ESLint 9 flat eslint.config.js using JS, TypeScript, Svelte recommended rules and eslint-config-prettier. Generated/tool state is ignored. Added direct @eslint/js and globals dev dependencies. Fixed the 10 real source violations instead of disabling recommended rules. bun run lint passes.
close_reason: ESLint 9 flat config and project-wide Prettier workflow are working; lint, tests, build, and diff checks pass.

title: Logout does not evict the in-memory session cache
description: src/hooks.server.ts caches {session,user} in a module-level object keyed by session id and returns it without revalidating. logout/+page.server.ts calls lucia.invalidateSession and clears the cookie but never deletes the cache entry, so a replayed cookie stays authenticated against the same warm edge instance. The cache is also never evicted on expiry and has no size bound.
design: delete sessionAndUserInfo[sessionId] on logout, and store expiry alongside the entry so stale ones are skipped.
acceptance_criteria: Log in, log out, replay the old cookie against the same running server: redirects to / , not /record.

title: Soft delete is logged as a review, inflating streak and heatmap
description: deleteCard (src/lib/db/tables/card.table.ts:85) is a db.update, so the log_card_update trigger in migrations/0001_plain_stingray.sql writes an activity row with action='UPDATE'. getCardsReviewed counts every 'UPDATE' row, so deleting cards raises the streak and paints the heatmap. log_card_delete never fires at all because nothing does a hard DELETE.
design: Add WHEN NEW.deleted = OLD.deleted to log_card_update, or have it write 'DELETE' when NEW.deleted=1. New migration, do not edit 0001 in place.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a card adds no activity row with action='UPDATE'. Streak on /measure does not move after a delete.

title: Add OAuth-compliant privacy disclosure
description: Google rejected Remember Forever branding because the homepage points its privacy-policy field back to the homepage and does not disclose data handling. Add a public privacy page that accurately describes Google profile data, flashcards, analytics, AI input sharing, cookies, retention, deletion contact, and link it from the public homepage.
acceptance_criteria: A public /privacy page explains how Google user data is accessed, used, stored, and shared; the homepage links to it; the route renders without authentication or JavaScript.
close_reason: Made signed-out navigation open by default, including mobile/no-JS rendering, while keeping privacy absent from signed-in links. Added regression coverage for open no-JS-style mobile navigation and reactive close after sign-in; targeted tests and production no-JS build pass.

title: Lucia is deprecated: decide between the single-file replacement and Better Auth
description:
lucia 3.2.0 and @lucia-auth/adapter-sqlite are in package.json. Lucia was deprecated in March 2025 and is now a learning resource rather than a maintained package. Nothing is broken, but the auth layer sits on an unmaintained dependency.

TWO EXITS, with very different costs:

1. COPY THE SINGLE FILE. Lucia publishes a complete single-file replacement (code/auth_session.ts) and states explicitly that NO DATABASE MIGRATIONS ARE NECESSARY. The existing auth_user and user_session tables stay as they are. Cheapest path, and it removes the dependency without changing behaviour. Note the new implementation patches a timing attack and may invalidate existing sessions, which would sign everyone out once.

2. ADOPT BETTER AUTH. Actively maintained, plugin ecosystem, and it has a Device Authorization plugin implementing RFC 8628 where THIS APP acts as the authorization server (a remfo code entered on a remfo page), which is the pairing flow remfo-11v.3 would otherwise get from Google. Cost is much higher: Better Auth expects its own schema (user, session, account, verification) against this app's auth_user and user_session, so it is a DATA migration, not just a code swap. It also touches hooks.server.ts, the OAuth callback, and the sessionExists guard in every load function.

SEQUENCING: do NOT do either in service of the Kindle work. remfo-11v.3 is additive, about 20 lines, and touches nothing that currently works. Decide this separately so two unknowns are not being debugged at once.

IF BETTER AUTH IS EVER CHOSEN, remfo-11v.3's Google device client could be retired in favour of its device plugin, removing the 'TVs and Limited Input devices' OAuth client. That is a future consolidation, not a reason to migrate now.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision between the two exits, with the reasoning, and an issue filed for whichever is chosen.

title: Test that the add-card path stays at one DB round trip
description:
Nothing catches a serial round trip being added to a hot write path. remfo-87b happened silently and was only noticed by feel.

WHY WALL-CLOCK THRESHOLDS ARE THE WRONG TEST: local latency (~300ms per round trip, California to Mumbai) and production latency (~2ms) differ by two orders of magnitude, so any fixed millisecond budget is either meaningless locally or impossible in CI. Measure ROUND TRIPS, not milliseconds.

TWO DESIGNS, pick one:
1. Ratio-based, no new machinery. In one run, measure a single round trip via the existing ?__dbping (hooks.server.ts), then measure submit-to-rendered-page for an add. Assert the ratio is under about 2. Environment-independent because both halves are measured on the same link, and the high local latency actually makes an extra trip easy to see.
2. Count queries directly. Wrap or instrument turso_client to count execute() calls per request and assert the add path issues the expected number. More precise and not timing-dependent, but needs instrumentation that must not ship to production.

GOTCHAS ALREADY PAID FOR, do not rediscover them:
- The POST needs an Origin header matching the preview origin, or SvelteKit's CSRF check refuses it in ~2ms with no card created, which looks exactly like a very fast add.
- Created cards CANNOT be removed afterwards (see remfo-bpt); the delete trigger makes DELETE FROM card fail. Clean up with a soft delete, UPDATE card SET deleted = 1, and accept that rows accumulate.
- scripts/session.mjs already handles env loading, minting a session with a 30-day expiry, and cleanup. Reuse it.
- It cannot live in the vitest suite, since bun run build runs the tests and this needs a built app. It belongs beside scripts/nojs.mjs as its own npm script.
acceptance_criteria: A committed check that fails when the add path gains an extra serial database round trip, verified by a mutation (reintroduce the awaited load and watch it fail).

title: Adding a card costs two serial DB round trips since /record awaits its load
description:
REPORTED: adding a new card feels far slower than before.

CAUSE, traced and almost certainly mine (remfo-11v.4): addAction (card.action.ts) inserts the card, then redirects to /record, whose load now AWAITS loadCards. So the submit-to-rendered-page path went from ONE serial database round trip (insert; the list streamed in afterwards) to TWO (insert, then the list query before anything renders).

MAGNITUDE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHERE IT IS FELT, and this needs confirming before any fix:
- Locally the dev machine is in California and the dev database is in aws-ap-south-1, so a round trip is ~300ms. Going from one to two is ~300ms to ~600ms, very noticeable.
- In production both function and database are in Mumbai and a round trip is ~2ms (measured, remfo-uze). Two trips is ~4ms, which should be imperceptible.
So this may be a development-environment artifact rather than a user-facing regression. ASK FIRST: was the slowness observed on www.remfo.app or on localhost? That determines whether this is a real bug or a dev-only annoyance.

IF IT IS REAL IN PRODUCTION, options: accept it (~2ms), or have the add action return the new card so the redirect target does not need to re-query, or reinstate streaming for /record only (which would break the no-JS card list again, so no).

MEASUREMENT GOTCHAS discovered while probing this, worth not rediscovering:
- SvelteKit rejects form POSTs without a matching Origin header (CSRF). A probe must send origin: http://localhost:4173 or it is refused in ~2ms with no card created, which looks deceptively like a fast add.
- Probe cards CANNOT be cleaned up by deletion. See the separate trigger issue. Soft delete them instead.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on whether this is user-facing, based on a production measurement of the add path rather than a local one.
notes:
MEASURED IN A BROWSER, which shows the user-visible shape of this.

  JS on : new card visible after 636ms, document NOT reloaded (0 load events, a window value survived) => client-side navigation
  JS off: new card visible after 784ms, document reloaded (1 load event) => genuine full page refresh

WHY IT FEELS WORSE with JS even though there is no reload: during a client-side navigation SvelteKit keeps the OLD page on screen until the new load resolves. load now awaits the card list, so nothing visibly changes for the duration of BOTH round trips (insert, then list query). The form clears instantly via customEnhance's optimistic reset, then the UI sits still.

Before remfo-11v.4, the navigation completed quickly because load returned a streamed promise, and the 'shown' cache kept the previous list rendered while the new one arrived, so the update felt immediate.

Local round trips are ~300ms and production round trips are ~2ms, so this should be ~10-20ms for real users. Confirm on production before changing anything.

Probe cards created during this measurement were soft-deleted.

title: Evaluate embedded replicas, which needs leaving the edge runtime
description:
Turso embedded replicas keep a full local SQLite replica synced against the remote primary: reads run at filesystem speed (microseconds), writes sync asynchronously. That would remove the 256ms round trip entirely, for BOTH the session lookup and the page query, rather than relocating it the way region pinning does.

BLOCKER: embedded replicas need a filesystem. Vercel's edge runtime is a V8 isolate and has none. Using them means moving svelte.config.js from runtime 'edge' to the Node serverless runtime. Turso's own Vercel Marketplace integration is built on exactly this pattern.

COSTS to weigh: replica lag on reads, cold starts, and CLAUDE.md's current rule that server code must avoid Node-only APIs (which would no longer apply, and is worth updating if this lands).

SEQUENCING: do NOT start this before remfo-uze (region pinning) is deployed and measured. That is one line and may reduce 256ms enough that this architectural change is not worth it. This issue only earns its keep if the region pin leaves meaningful latency behind.

ALSO CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: libSQL batch(). It packs statements into one round trip, but /record's two queries are already concurrent via Promise.all so wall-clock is already one trip, and batched statements cannot consume each other's results, so it cannot merge the auth-then-query dependency either.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision, with post-region-pin numbers, on whether to move to the Node serverless runtime with embedded replicas.
notes:
ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT WORTH DOING, per the acceptance condition set on this issue.

The premise was removing a 256ms round trip. After remfo-uze that round trip is 2ms, measured in production. Embedded replicas would trade 2ms for sync bandwidth billing, cold-start hydration of the whole database on every new serverless instance, replica staleness, and abandoning the edge runtime. Nothing left to win.
close_reason: Premise removed. The round trip embedded replicas would eliminate is now 2ms after the connection-string fix.

title: No-JS render: cover /measure and /record, and guard with a test
description:
Two parts, folded together per decision.

PART 1, fix: /measure and /record still use the streamed-load pattern that remfo-11v.1 removed from /revise, so both are still blank without JS. measure/+page.svelte streams data.reviewedInfo and data.recordedInfo; record/+page.svelte streams data.cards. Apply the same await change, and measure each page before/after with 'bun run perf --pages <page> --label ...' rather than assuming /revise's result transfers. /revise won because the card was the LCP element; these pages have different content and the numbers may differ.

PART 2, guard: nothing tests the no-JS path, which is why the regression went unnoticed while CLAUDE.md claims 'App should work well without JS'. Without a guard the next streamed load reintroduces it.

Reference for the proof technique: remfo-11v.1 verified this by minting a user_session row directly (same shape as scripts/perf.mjs), fetching the built preview with that cookie, and asserting the card text appears in the raw HTML. A '.resolve(' script in the response is the tell that data is being delivered JS-only.
acceptance_criteria: /revise, /measure and /record each render their primary content in the server HTML with no JS. A test fails if any protected page's primary content is absent from the server-rendered HTML. Before/after perf numbers recorded for /measure and /record.
notes:
COMPLETE. /record now awaits its list, and the guard covers all three protected pages.

DECIDED ON PRODUCTION NUMBERS, not the misleading local ones: /record's shell is 2ms WHILE STREAMING, meaning the shell returns before the query, and that query now costs ~2-5ms after remfo-uze. Streaming was buying single-digit milliseconds in exchange for a card list that only existed for JS clients.

KEPT DELIBERATELY: the failure branch. A naive await would turn a Turso outage into a full error page. load now does .catch(() => null) and the page renders 'could not load your cards.' beside a working add form, which is what the old {:catch} provided. Removing streaming should not remove error handling.

DELETED: the 'shown' previous-list cache, which existed only because a re-run load handed the page a fresh pending promise. With an awaited load SvelteKit keeps the old page rendered until the new load resolves, so it has no job left.

TESTS: record/page.test.ts rewritten from 4 streaming tests to 2 that match reality, since only two states can now reach the component. The second asserts the add form survives a failed load.

GUARD: /record added to scripts/nojs.mjs, keyed on 'showing N of M cards', which NewCards renders only once the list is in hand, so it cannot pass on a shell. MUTATION CHECKED by reintroducing the streaming: reported 'missing the card list' and 'still has a streamed-promise resolve() script', 23243 bytes vs 169587 working.

GATES: 46/46 tests, test:nojs passes all three pages, prettier clean, svelte-check unchanged at 12 pre-existing errors. One eslint error remains in PrimaryNav.svelte, pre-existing and filed as remfo-2nd.
close_reason: /record awaited with its failure branch preserved, tests rewritten, and the no-JS guard now covers all three protected pages with a mutation check.

title: Google device flow (RFC 8628) sign-in for browsers Google rejects
description:
Google's normal sign-in page refuses the Kindle browser and that cannot be fixed from this repo. The earlier plan was a hand-rolled pairing code. That is now SUPERSEDED: OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628) is a standard for exactly this, Google implements it, and it removes every hand-built piece.

WHAT GOOGLE OWNS INSTEAD OF US: the code and its format, entropy, expiry (returned as expires_in), and brute-force rate limiting. No pairing_code table, no custom credential that mints a session.

BETTER UX TOO: the Kindle only DISPLAYS the code, and the user types it on their phone at Google's verification URL. The earlier design had them typing on an e-ink keyboard.

VERIFIED AGAINST GOOGLE'S DOCS (developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/limited-input-device):
- Device flow is restricted to a short scope list, and openid/email/profile are on it. This app requests ['profile','email'], so it is inside that list.
- Step 1: POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/device/code with client_id and scope. Returns device_code, user_code, verification_url, interval, expires_in.
- Step 2: POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token with client_id, client_secret, device_code, grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code.
- While the user has not approved, Google returns HTTP 428 with error 'authorization_pending'.

NO-JS ADAPTATION: devices are meant to poll, which needs JS. Instead the page renders an 'I have approved it, continue' submit button that performs step 2. On authorization_pending it re-renders 'not approved yet, try again'. Plain form, no JS, no polling.

FITS THE EXISTING CODE: on success, feed the same insertOrUpdateGoogleUser + lucia.createSession path that (auth)/login/google/callback/+server.ts already uses. Carry device_code between the two requests in a short-lived httpOnly cookie, exactly the pattern login/google/+server.ts uses for google_oauth_state and google_oauth_code_verifier. No new table.

NO LIBRARY DOES THIS: arctic 1.9.2's Google provider exposes only createAuthorizationURL, validateAuthorizationCode and refreshAccessToken (checked in node_modules). Two fetch calls against documented endpoints, roughly 20 lines, no new dependency.

BLOCKED ON A HUMAN STEP: Google requires an OAuth client of application type 'TVs and Limited Input devices'. The existing Web application client WILL NOT WORK; the docs name a wrong client type as a specific error condition. Someone must create that client in Google Cloud Console, producing a new client id and secret, which become two new env vars.
acceptance_criteria: From a browser that never loads accounts.google.com and has JS disabled, displaying a Google user code and confirming approval on another device establishes a valid lucia session. Unapproved and expired codes are rejected with a message rather than an error page.
notes:
REVISED after visual review: the bounce state was rendering a bordered box with its own black button, which competed with the primary sign-in button and stacked two identical-looking calls to action. It is now a single quiet line of grey text below the primary button, in the same position in both states, differing only in wording. Screenshots taken of both.

AUTO-POLLING ADDED. Without JS the button is the only way forward and the person is the poll. With JS the page presses it for them on google's own interval, which is what a device with a real runtime would do. Implemented with use:enhance, so removing JS falls straight back to the plain form post.
- load now returns intervalSeconds (google's `interval`, default 5) and expiresAt
- slow_down is honoured per RFC 8628: the action reports it and the page widens its interval by 5s
- polling stops once the code has expired instead of running forever

VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER against the built preview:
- JS on : 2 automatic POSTs in 13 seconds at google's 5s interval, with no click; the status message updates and the code on screen does not change
- JS off: the button still works, the status still appears, the code is still preserved

TESTS: 53 total. Two new polling tests, both MUTATION CHECKED:
- removing the initial schedulePoll call fails "resubmits on google's interval"
- removing the expiry guard fails "stops once the code has expired", which matters because that test asserts a negative and would otherwise pass even if polling never worked

GATES: 53/53 tests, test:nojs passes all four pages, prettier clean, svelte-check back to the pre-existing 12 (it hit 13 because the test fixture's form object no longer matched ActionData once slowDown was added).

comments.author: Sanyam Jain
comments.text: Google's documented device-code request accepts only client_id and scope; it provides no account-type or login_hint control. The google.com/device chooser may offer Brand Accounts, and Remfo cannot suppress that UI. Removing it requires replacing Google Device Authorization Grant with a Remfo-owned pairing flow that authenticates the phone through the existing normal Google web flow.

title: Reveal card answer without hover or JS
description: Card.svelte:44 hides the answer with 'blur-md hover:filter-none'. E-ink has no hover, so the answer is unreachable on Kindle. Replace with <details>/<summary>, which needs no JS. Known risk: the Kindle browser is old WebKit and may not support <details>; unsupported browsers render the content always-visible, turning the card into a cheat sheet. That failure is silent and only detectable on the device.
acceptance_criteria: With JS disabled, the answer is hidden on load and revealed by activating the summary. Keyboard reachable. Regression test covers it.
notes:
HOVER RESTORED. Dropping hover was a UX regression: the desktop design was zero-click, just move the pointer over the card.

Card.svelte <style>, inside the existing @supports block:
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { details:not([open]):hover > .answer-body { filter: none; user-select: auto } }

Hover is now the enhancement and <details> is the floor, which is the inverse of the original code where hover was the ONLY mechanism and therefore dead on touch, keyboard and e-ink.

VERIFIED matrix against the built preview in real Chrome (hover-capable | at rest | pointer over | via summary):
  desktop mouse, JS on   true  | blur(6px) | none      | none, open
  desktop mouse, JS off  true  | blur(6px) | none      | none, open
  touch/e-ink, JS on     false | blur(6px) | blur(6px) | none, open
  touch/e-ink, JS off    false | blur(6px) | blur(6px) | none, open
Hover reveal now works with JS disabled, which it never did before.

VERIFICATION GOTCHA, worth remembering: CDP Emulation.setEmulatedMedia with hover/pointer features is SILENTLY IGNORED in this Chrome (matchMedia reports hover:hover under both settings), so the touch branch appeared broken when it was not. Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled + setDeviceMetricsOverride({mobile:true}) does flip the media query correctly. Use that.
close_reason: details/summary reveal shipped with a mutation-checked regression test and SSR proof. Old-WebKit support risk recorded, testable only on the device.

title: Measure: await vs stream cards on /revise
description: Streaming /revise gives a fast empty shell but the card is the LCP element and arrives late. Latest mobile run: FCP 1.6s, LCP 3.7s. Awaiting the cards in load may lower LCP AND fix the no-JS render for free, deleting the streaming complexity instead of working around it. Decide the no-JS render approach from the numbers, not from assumption.
acceptance_criteria: Lighthouse LCP/FCP for /revise recorded for both streamed and awaited variants, mobile and desktop, 3 runs each. A decision is recorded on the parent epic.
notes:
MEASURED, 3 runs each, localhost preview, Turso remote (getCards ~415ms).

              FCP        LCP       TTFB
desktop stream  285ms     573ms       4ms
desktop await   313ms     463ms     434ms
mobile  stream 1311ms    3298ms     288ms
mobile  await  1031ms    1307ms     695ms

DECISION: delete the streaming on /revise. Streaming bought a fast TTFB and paid a 2s worse LCP on mobile. Awaiting wins FCP and LCP on mobile and LCP on desktop, for a 28ms desktop FCP cost. TTFB regresses as expected and does not matter here.

NO-JS VERIFIED both directions against the built preview with a minted session:
- streamed: html 23582 bytes, no id="question", no card text, a '.resolve(' script present (the JS-only delivery path, kit render.js:569)
- awaited:  html 28291 bytes, card front AND back both present

Gates: bun run test 46/46 pass. bun run check shows 12 errors, all pre-existing on main (verified by stashing).

NOT DONE: /measure and /record still use the same streamed pattern and are still blank without JS.
close_reason: Measured, decided, and the await change is applied to /revise with before/after no-JS proof.

title: Kindle: no-JS render, hover-free reveal, and Google-free auth
description:
Kindle (no-JS, old WebKit) cannot complete a review. Google's sign-in page rejects the Kindle browser, but auth is only the first of three walls. Confirmed: (1) /revise streams cards via an unawaited load promise; SvelteKit delivers resolution through an inline <script> (kit render.js:569), so with no JS the page renders empty. Same pattern in /measure and /record. (2) The answer is hidden behind 'blur-md hover:filter-none' (Card.svelte:44); e-ink has no hover, so the answer can never be revealed. (3) Google sign-in is unusable on that browser and cannot be fixed from this repo.

Acceptance: on the Kindle, reach /revise, review a card, and the answer persists, without touching a Google page.

Decisions taken: target is no-JS (not old-JS polyfilling). Reveal via <details>/<summary>. Auth via pairing code, phone displays the code, Kindle types it into a plain form (no polling, no email dependency). Lucia session default is 30 days sliding (no sessionExpiresIn set), so pairing recurs about monthly.

title: add formatting/lintinting to db queries so i don't have to scroll horizontally a lot and its easier to read the db query

title: add dark theme
make http://localhost:5173/record load instantly, once user is signed in
description:
/record is slow for signed-in users. Two independent causes, measured 2026-08-31.

CAUSE 1 - sequential Turso round trips before first byte (~600ms).
Measured RTT from dev machine to the Turso host: ~300ms per query, warm ('select 1' = 299-408ms).
Per request: hooks.server.ts validateSession (adapter runs 2 queries in Promise.all = 1 RTT) then
record/+page.server.ts awaits getCardsOrderByCreated (1 RTT). Sequential, because the card query
needs userId from the session. Lucia also fires updateSessionExpiration past the session half-life,
a 3rd RTT. The module-level sessionAndUserInfo cache in hooks.server.ts removes the first RTT only
on a warm edge instance.
The SQL itself is NOT the cost: getCardsOrderByCreated measured 335-354ms warm, i.e. ~35-50ms above
the pure network floor, on 1373 total rows.

CAUSE 2 - unbounded payload and DOM (the bigger one for the owner account).
No LIMIT on getCardsOrderByCreated. Top account has 1005 cards. NewCards.svelte renders every one,
each with ~2KB of template (measured 2067 bytes for the per-card block), 2 forms and 2 inline SVGs.
So roughly 1.5-2MB of HTML plus the same card data again in the hydration payload, ~2000 forms and
~2000 inline SVGs in the DOM. Estimated from template size, not from a captured response.

NOT the cause (checked, do not chase):
- Missing index. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN confirms 'SCAN card' + 'USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY' (card has
  no index beyond the id autoindex), but at 1373 rows it costs ~40ms. Worth adding
  card(user_id, deleted, created_at) for the future, not for this bead.

FIX ORDER (largest win first):
1. Paginate / LIMIT the card query - see remfo-i84. Kills both payload and DOM cost.
2. Stream: return the getCardsOrderByCreated promise unawaited from load so the shell renders after
   the session RTT instead of after both. Needs {#await} in +page.svelte.
3. Index card(user_id, deleted, created_at).

Related: remfo-i84 (pagination), remfo-9s7 (session cache is not evicted on logout - same cache).
notes: Implemented the measured main optimizations on 2026-08-31. Added and applied migration 0003_clean_husk with index card(user_id, deleted, created_at). Replaced cards + exact COUNT queries with one indexed LIMIT+1 query returning hasMore; UI now says showing N cards and retains load-more behavior. Streaming and 50-card pagination remain. Isolated 3-run mobile benchmark: average observed load 680ms, TTFB 255ms; versus the prior one-run isolated baseline load 1166ms/TTFB 842ms (directionally 42%/70% better, baseline sample is not statistically equivalent). Compared with the temporary COUNT OVER implementation, load/FCP/LCP improved 7% and TTFB 12%. Card query still takes 377-438ms, approximately one Turso network RTT. The 100ms budget still fails and cannot be reached from this dev machine without colocating app+DB, a nearby embedded/read replica, or serving cached/stale user data. Tests 47 pass and production build passes. Existing repository svelte-check still fails with 21 unrelated diagnostics in shortcuts/hooks/heatmap/PWA declarations.
close_reason: Implemented page-level main optimizations: bounded streamed pagination, indexed LIMIT+1 query, no exact-count request, and applied migration. Remaining latency is tracked as infrastructure colocation/caching work.

title: Streak drops to 0 at midnight instead of at end of day
description: calculateStreak in src/lib/algo.utils.ts counts back from the date it is given and stops at the first day with no activity - starting with today. So the moment the local day rolls over, a user who reviewed daily for 100 days sees 'Current Streak: 0' until their first review of the new day. Most streak UIs keep yesterday's streak displayed until that day actually ends. Pinned as-is by the test 'is 0 when yesterday was active but today is not' in src/lib/algo.util.test.ts rather than silently changed, because it is a product decision.
design: Start the walk at yesterday when today has no activity, i.e. allow one day of grace before the streak reads 0. Roughly: if the set has no entry for today, begin the countdown at today-1.
acceptance_criteria: A user who reviewed yesterday but not yet today still sees their streak; it only reaches 0 after a full day with no activity.

title: cal-heatmap is 114KB, 43% unused, ES5-transpiled - the only thing keeping /measure off 100
description: Measured on production /measure mobile, 2026-08-28 16:46 (post-deploy, a11y now 100). nodes/6.js is 113,963 bytes transferred, 43% unused (49KB), and legacy-javascript-insight finds 24KB of @babel/plugin-transform-classes, transform-regenerator and transform-spread inside it - cal-heatmap ships an ES5 bundle while the Vite build targets modern browsers. Main-thread work is 1.1s of which script evaluation is 654ms and style/layout only 72ms, so this page is JS-bound and the JS is one dependency. cal-heatmap@4.2.4 is already the latest published version, so no upgrade fixes this. It also adds a third render-blocking stylesheet (6.ClhAfimw.css, 759B) and is the likely cause of the 0.037 CLS seen on desktop.
design: Cheapest: dynamic-import Heatmap.svelte from HeatmapCard.svelte, same technique that took the root layout chunk from 176KB to 23KB for posthog, plus a fixed-height wrapper div to kill the CLS. Keeps the feature. Bigger: drop cal-heatmap and render 365 squares with CSS grid from the existing getCardsGroupedByActivityDate query - roughly 30 lines, removes the app's largest dependency, but means reimplementing month labels, the colour scale and tooltips.
acceptance_criteria: /measure mobile performance 100 at median of 3+ runs; nodes/6.js no longer on the critical path.

title: measure tab not looks good on mobile
ContentRenderer probed every card URL over the network, leaking card URLs to third parties
description: FIXED in this session; filed for the record and for the deploy check. src/lib/components/ContentRenderer.svelte decided whether card text was an image by assigning it to new Image().src, which issued a real cross-origin request for every URL card. On /revise with ~800 cards due, Lighthouse (2026-08-28, production) recorded third-party cookies from youtube.com (including the __Secure-3PSID auth cookie), en.wikipedia.org and leetcode.com, dropping best-practices to 77 on both desktop and mobile, plus Cookie entries in inspector-issues. It was also a privacy leak: each user's saved URLs were pinged from their browser on every review session, and the probe always failed for HTML pages after paying full network cost. Replaced with a pathname extension check, so no request is made. Also restricted hrefs to http/https, since card text is user input rendered into an href and a javascript: card would previously have produced a live javascript: link.
design: Tradeoff: extension-less image URLs (CDN links without a file extension) now render as links rather than images. A HEAD request would restore that, at the cost of reintroducing a per-card network call. Marked with a ponytail: comment in the file.
acceptance_criteria: Rerun Lighthouse on /revise after deploy: third-party-cookies and inspector-issues pass, best-practices back to 100, TBT improves from 740ms mobile.
close_reason: Fixed: ContentRenderer now classifies URLs by pathname extension instead of loading them, and restricts hrefs to http/https. Tests added in src/lib/components/ContentRenderer.test.ts. Verify against production after deploy.

title: /record renders every card with no LIMIT: 819 cards = 161KB of HTML
description: Measured by Lighthouse against production /record on 2026-08-28 with 819 cards. getCardsOrderByCreated in src/lib/db/tables/card.table.ts has no LIMIT and no pagination, so every visit server-renders the user's entire card history. Mobile results: perf 93 (vs 100 on the logged-out landing page), FCP 1.9s, LCP 2.3s, TBT 210ms. The HTML document alone is 161KB, larger than every JS chunk combined; total page weight 289KB. Main-thread work is 1.7s of which Style and Layout is 408ms and script evaluation only 242ms, which is the signature of an oversized DOM rather than slow JS. Desktop still scores 100, so this is currently mobile-only and degrades as the card count grows. Note src/routes/(protected)/revise/+page.server.ts has the same unbounded shape via getCardsOrderByNextPractice, though it is filtered by nextPractice < now so it grows more slowly.
design: Options, cheapest first: (1) LIMIT + offset or cursor pagination in getCardsOrderByCreated, needs a UI affordance on /record; (2) virtualize the list client-side, keeps one query but still ships 161KB of HTML; (3) infinite scroll on top of (1). Pagination at the query is the root-cause fix since it shrinks both the SQL result and the SSR payload.
acceptance_criteria: /record HTML payload stays roughly constant as card count grows. Mobile Lighthouse performance back to 100 at 800+ cards. Deleting and adding cards still lands the user on a correct list.

title: upgrade packages
No tests for calculateSuperMemo2Algorithm
description: The SM-2 scheduler in card.table.ts is the core of the product and has zero tests. Existing suite is 3 files: index.test.ts is expect(1+2).toBe(3), algo.util.test.ts covers streak math, CardReview.test.ts covers the review component. No server load or action is tested. @vitest/coverage-v8 is installed but there is no coverage script.
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert interval progression 1 then 6 then round(interval*easiness), reset to 1 on quality<3, and easiness floor of 1.3. bun run test green.
close_reason: Done. Moved calculateSuperMemo2Algorithm out of card.table.ts into src/lib/algo.utils.ts (card.table.ts is query functions only per CLAUDE.md, and it could not be imported under test because it constructs the Turso client at module load). src/lib/algo.util.test.ts now covers SM-2 interval progression, repetition reset on failing grades, all four easiness deltas, the 1.3 floor, nextPractice under fake timers, the mutate-and-return contract reviewCard depends on, and a six-review integration sequence; plus rewritten streak tests including the previously skipped one. 42 tests pass. Suite mutation-checked against 5 seeded defects, each caught.

title: record and measure loads use locals.user! with no session guard
description: record/+page.server.ts:13 and measure/+page.server.ts:4-5 dereference locals.user! . In SvelteKit the (protected)/+layout.server.ts guard runs in parallel with page loads, not before, so an unauthenticated request can throw a TypeError before the redirect lands. revise and learn already do this correctly with sessionExists.
design: Use sessionExists(locals) from src/lib/common.util.ts, same shape as revise/+page.server.ts.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthenticated GET /record and /measure redirect to / instead of 500.

title: /measure heatmap does not render without JS
description:
Heatmap.svelte builds the grid with cal-heatmap inside onMount, so on a client with no JS the heatmap is blank. The surrounding page IS server-rendered: Streak shows 'Current Streak: N' and HeatmapCard shows 'N cards reviewed' / 'N cards created', which is why scripts/nojs.mjs passes /measure. Those assertions are honest about the page loading and the data resolving, but they do NOT prove the principal visual renders.

So /measure is partially functional on a Kindle: the numbers are there, the grid is not.

OPTIONS: server-render a simple grid (a table or CSS grid of divs, one per day, coloured by count) and let cal-heatmap remain a progressive enhancement for JS clients; or accept the degraded state and say so in the guard's comments so the next reader is not misled.

NOT A BLOCKER for the epic's acceptance, which is about /revise. Filed so the gap is recorded rather than hidden behind a passing check.
acceptance_criteria: Either the heatmap grid appears in server-rendered HTML, or the nojs guard documents explicitly that /measure's grid is JS-only.

title: log_card_delete trigger makes hard-deleting a card impossible
description:
migrations/0001_plain_stingray.sql defines log_card_delete AFTER DELETE ON card, which INSERTs an activity row with card_id = OLD.id. activity.card_id has a foreign key to card.id, so the trigger writes a reference to the row that was just removed and the statement fails with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed.

The result is that DELETE FROM card can never succeed. Reproduced while cleaning up probe rows: deleting the activity rows first does not help, because the trigger inserts a new one during the delete.

The application never hits this because deletes are soft (card.deleted = true), so it is latent rather than breaking. It does block anything that needs a genuine hard delete: test fixture cleanup, purging probe data, an account-erasure or GDPR path, or trimming the table.

Options: drop the trigger's FK dependency by making activity.card_id a plain column, or drop the DELETE trigger since the app never hard-deletes, or make it ON DELETE CASCADE from activity to card so the row goes away instead of being logged.
acceptance_criteria: Either hard deletes work, or a recorded decision that the app is soft-delete-only and the DELETE trigger is removed as dead and misleading.

title: Collapse session validation and page query into one round trip
description:
Follow-on to the region pinning. hooks.server.ts validates the session, then load runs its query, serially, because load needs locals.user.id. That is two round trips where one would do: a single statement joining user_session to the page's table returns both the user and the rows.

Halves whatever latency remains after the region fix. More invasive than that fix because it routes around lucia for the read path, so only worth doing once the region change is measured and the remaining cost is known.
acceptance_criteria: Protected pages issue one database round trip per request instead of two, measured via Server-Timing.
notes: Not worth doing after remfo-uze. This proposed merging two serial round trips into one. Those round trips are now 2ms each in production, so the entire saving is about 2ms in exchange for routing around lucia for the read path. Closing unless a future measurement shows otherwise.
close_reason: Saving is ~2ms after the connection-string fix. Not worth routing around lucia.

title: Delete unused reviewForm from revise load
description:
revise/+page.server.ts creates 'const reviewForm = superValidate(zod(cardReviewSchema))' and returns it, but nothing anywhere consumes data.reviewForm (grep across src finds only these two lines). It is returned unawaited, so it is still a streamed promise: after the remfo-11v.1 fix the SSR html for /revise STILL contains a '.resolve(' script, purely for a value no component reads.

Deleting it removes the last deferred promise from the page and makes the no-JS story on /revise complete. Relevant to remfo-11v.4: a test asserting 'no .resolve( script' would fail today for this reason alone, so either delete this first or assert on content presence instead.
acceptance_criteria: reviewForm removed, nothing references it, tests green, and /revise SSR html contains no '.resolve(' script.
close_reason: reviewForm and its now-unused superValidate/zod/cardReviewSchema imports removed. reviewAction builds its own form from the event, so nothing depended on it. Verified: /revise SSR html now contains no '.resolve(' script, card still renders, 48/48 tests, build green.

title: Logo link has no accessible name
description: PrimaryNav.svelte:49 - an <a href="/"> containing only an <enhanced:img> with no accessible name. Surfaced as a new warning by svelte 5.57 (svelte.dev/e/a11y_consider_explicit_label); older prerelease did not report it. Screen reader users hear the image filename or nothing instead of a link purpose. CLAUDE.md requires accessibility best practices.
acceptance_criteria: The link has an accessible name (alt text on the image, or aria-label on the link). svelte-check reports no a11y warning for it.

title: Upgraded svelte to 5.57.0 stable and vitest to 2.1.9
description:
DONE, recorded for context. package.json: svelte 5.0.0-next.195 -> 5.57.0, vitest 1.6.0 -> 2.1.9, @vitest/ui ^2.0.4 -> 2.0.5 (it was mismatched against vitest 1.6.0). Off a two-year-old prerelease.

ISOLATION EXPERIMENT, so this is not repeated:
- happy-dom 20 alone: 4 tests fail, all 'click a review button advances the card'. customEnhance never runs (progress bar stuck at width:0.00%).
- svelte 5.57 stable + vitest 2 + happy-dom 20: same 4 failures. Svelte prerelease was NOT the cause.
- svelte 5.57 stable + vitest 2 + happy-dom 14: 48/48 green.
CONCLUSION: happy-dom 20 breaks Svelte's use:enhance. Nothing to do with Svelte's version.
- vitest 4 is unreachable without upgrading vite: it needs vite >=6 and this repo is on vite 5.3.4, which would drag in the whole build toolchain (kit, vite-plugin-pwa, unplugin-icons). vitest 2 works on vite 5, which is why it was chosen.

VERIFIED after the upgrade: 48/48 tests, build green, svelte-check still 12 errors (unchanged from main) plus 1 new warning (filed separately), and /revise re-verified in real Chrome with JS both on and off.

NOT UPGRADED, deliberately: @sveltejs/kit stays 2.5.18 (2.70.3 exists, 65 minors behind) to avoid widening scope, and happy-dom stays 14.
close_reason: Upgrade applied and verified; issue exists to record the isolation experiment.

title: Remove unused cypress
description: cypress ^13.13.1 is a devDependency with cypress.config.ts and a single untouched template spec (cypress/e2e/spec.cy.ts visits example.cypress.io). There is no npm script for it and it has never been run. It is also the wrong tool for this repo's main testing gap: Cypress requires JS in the page to drive the test, so it cannot verify the no-JS rendering that CLAUDE.md promises.
acceptance_criteria: cypress, cypress.config.ts and cypress/ removed, suite still green. Or a recorded reason to keep it.

title: happy-dom 14 to 20 breaks use:enhance in tests
description:
happy-dom is pinned at ^14.12.3, six majors behind 20.12.0. Upgrading gains real HTMLDetailsElement semantics (verified on 20: 'open' is false initially and clicking summary flips it to true), which would let CardReview.test.ts assert actual disclosure behaviour instead of only the markup contract.

Attempted and reverted. On happy-dom 20, 4 tests fail (3 pre-existing): every test where clicking a review button should advance the card. The progress bar stays at width:0.00%, so customEnhance never runs at all. Form submit events DO still fire on happy-dom 20 (checked in isolation), so the break is deeper, in the interaction between happy-dom 20's SubmitEvent and Svelte's use:enhance on the pinned Svelte 5 prerelease (5.0.0-next.195).

Also noted: vitest is 1.6.0 while @vitest/ui is ^2.0.4, already mismatched.

Low priority. This only improves unit-level fidelity for <details>. It does NOT help the no-JS render guarantee (see remfo-11v.4), because every DOM library executes JS.
acceptance_criteria: happy-dom upgraded with the full suite green, or a recorded decision to stay on 14 with the reason.
close_reason: Investigated. happy-dom 20 is the sole cause of the use:enhance breakage, isolated by experiment. Staying on 14; the reachable part of the upgrade (svelte stable, vitest 2) was taken instead.

title: Streaks are bucketed in the runtime's local timezone, not the user's
description: Both calculateStreak and calculateMaxStreak bucket activity with toLocaleDateString('en-CA'), which uses whatever timezone the code happens to run in. The activity table stores UTC (the SQL triggers use strftime('%s','now')), and Streak.svelte runs during SSR on Vercel edge (UTC) as well as in the user's browser (their local zone), so the same data can produce different streaks on the server-rendered page and after hydration. It also means a review at 23:00 in UTC+5:30 lands on the previous day when bucketed in UTC. This was why the original 'should calculate max streak' test was skipped: it asserted startDate '2020-12-31' for a UTC-midnight input, which only holds in a timezone behind UTC. The replacement tests in src/lib/algo.util.test.ts derive expected dates through the same conversion so they pass in any zone, but that makes them timezone-agnostic, not timezone-correct.
design: Decide whose day boundary counts - almost certainly the user's - then bucket consistently against it: store or pass an IANA timezone and convert once, rather than relying on the ambient zone of whichever runtime executes the function.
acceptance_criteria: A given activity set produces the same streak on the server and in the browser, and day boundaries follow the user's timezone.

title: Re-measure /measure mobile: LCP moved 2.7s to 3.2s after the posthog lazy-load
description: Single-run comparison on production /measure mobile: before deploy (16:39) LCP 2.7s, TTI 2.7s, perf 93. After deploy (16:46) LCP 3.2s, TTI 3.2s, perf 90 - while FCP improved 1.0s to 0.9s and Speed Index improved 2.1s to 1.6s, and total page weight was identical at 241 KiB. Early paint got better, LCP and TTI got worse. Two candidate causes that one run each cannot separate: (a) ordinary run-to-run variance in simulated throttling, where LCP swings of half a second are normal; (b) a real effect, since posthog is still fetched, now as a 48KB chunk competing for bandwidth during load instead of before it - unused-javascript estimated savings rose from 280ms to 450ms.
design: If real, the fix is to defer posthog past load rather than to onMount: requestIdleCallback, or initialise it only on the routes whose events are actually used.
acceptance_criteria: Median of 5 runs on /measure mobile before and after, LCP compared on medians rather than single runs. Decide from that whether any change is warranted.

title: Accessibility: audit /learn, /measure and /revise with authenticated Lighthouse
description: Lighthouse has now covered / (logged out) and /record (819 cards). /revise, /learn and /measure remain unmeasured. /measure is the highest risk: its client chunk is 319KB, the largest in the build, because it bundles cal-heatmap - 1.8x larger than the root layout chunk that the earlier reports flagged. Also worth checking: the delete button in src/lib/components/Cards/Card.svelte (used on /revise) relies on title='move to trash' plus an empty for its accessible name. That satisfies axe's button-name rule so it will not fail the audit, but title is not exposed on touch devices and is deprioritised by screen readers; an explicit aria-label would be stronger.
acceptance_criteria: Lighthouse run with an authenticated session against /revise, /learn and /measure; findings triaged into beads.

title: tailwindcss 3 -> 4 migration
description: Verified from the v4 upgrade guide. CSS-first config (tailwind.config.ts only loads via an explicit @config directive), PostCSS plugin moves to @tailwindcss/postcss, @tailwind directives replaced by @import 'tailwindcss', removed utilities (bg-opacity-*, flex-shrink-*, flex-grow-*, overflow-ellipsis), renamed ones (shadow-sm -> shadow-xs, ring -> ring-3), default border color now currentColor, ! modifier moves to the end of the class, corePlugins option removed. Browser floor becomes Safari 16.4+ / Chrome 111+ / Firefox 128+. src/app.css and every component's classes are in scope.
acceptance_criteria: App renders identically on tailwind 4; no @tailwind directives left; postcss.config.js uses @tailwindcss/postcss.

title: arctic 1.9.2 -> 3.x is a breaking OAuth rewrite
description: Verified from arctic release notes. v2 breaking: createAuthorizationURL() no longer returns a Promise; validateAuthorizationCode() returns OAuth2Tokens instead of the old token object; it can now throw ArcticFetchError as well as OAuth2RequestError; scopes are no longer applied by default (including openid and provider-required ones); options.scope removed from createAuthorizationURL. v3 adds stricter RFC 6749 compliance. Affects src/lib/server/auth.ts and both files under src/routes/(auth)/login/google/.
acceptance_criteria: Google login end to end works on arctic 3: authorize redirect, callback, session created, profile+email scopes still granted.

acceptance_criteria: Auth runs on maintained code (own session table + cookie helpers per the Lucia v4 guide, or a supported alternative). Login, logout and session expiry all work.

Also happydom.ts + bunfig.toml + @happy-dom/global-registrator are leftovers from a 'bun test' experiment; the test script is vitest, which reads environment:'happy-dom' from vite.config.ts and resolves happy-dom only transitively. Empty dirs, ROUTES.ALL, commented-out code in card.table.ts and the cypress scaffold NOT done - split out.

title: Dependency upgrade sweep, everything is mid-2024
description: svelte pinned to prerelease 5.0.0-next.195, SvelteKit 2.5.18, vite 5.3.4, drizzle 0.32, vitest 1.6 while @vitest/ui and @vitest/coverage-v8 are on ^2 (a major ahead of the runner). No Dependabot or Renovate. Components use export let so the Svelte upgrade is mostly mechanical but untested.
design: These are not 50 independent bumps. One coupled chain, driven by peer deps verified against the registry: vitest 4 needs vite >=6; vite-plugin-svelte 7 needs vite 8 AND svelte >=5.46.4; @sveltejs/enhanced-img 0.11 needs vite >=6.3 and vite-plugin-svelte >=6. So svelte prerelease -> stable, vite 5->8, vite-plugin-svelte 3->7, vitest 1->4 (+ @vitest/ui to a matching 4.x), enhanced-img 0.3->0.11 and svelte-check 3->4 all move together or not at all. @sveltejs/kit stays on major 2 (2.5.18 -> 2.70.3) and adapter-vercel 5->6 only needs kit ^2.4. Hard stop: kit 2.70 peer-depends on typescript '^5.3.3 || ^6.0.0', so TypeScript 7.0 is OFF the table until kit allows it; go to TS 5.9/6 at most. Independent of that chain: tailwind 3->4 (CSS-first config, @tailwindcss/postcss, @import instead of @tailwind, renamed utilities, Safari 16.4+/Chrome 111+ floor) is a real migration and should be its own task. zod 3->4 is mostly deprecations, but sveltekit-superforms 2.30 peers zod '^3.25 || ^4' and ships a separate zod4 adapter import path, so superforms and zod move together.
acceptance_criteria: svelte on a stable release, vitest and its plugins on matching majors, bun run test and check green, Dependabot or Renovate config committed.
